title: Papadmalji Agro Foods IPO Details
intro:
Papadmalji Agro Foods IPO is a book build issue of ₹20.18 crores. The issue is a combination of fresh issue of 25.73 lakh shares aggregating to ₹18.52 crores and offer for sale of 2.30 lakh shares aggregating to ₹1.66 crores.

Papadmalji Agro Foods IPO opens for subscription on Sep 29, 2026 and closes on Oct 1, 2026. The allotment for the Papadmalji Agro Foods IPO is expected to be finalized on Oct 5, 2026. Papadmalji Agro Foods IPO will list on the NSE SME with a tentative listing date fixed as Oct 7, 2026.

Papadmalji Agro Foods IPO is set issue price band at ₹69 to ₹72 per share. The lot size for an application is 1,600 shares. The minimum amount of investment required by an individual investor (retail) is ₹2,30,400 (3,200 shares) (based on upper price). The minimum lot size for investment in HNI is 3 lots (4,800 shares), amounting to ₹3,45,600.

Kreo Capital Pvt.Ltd. is the book running lead manager and MAS Services Ltd. is the registrar of the issue. The Market Maker of the company is Giriraj Stock Broking Pvt.Ltd.

Refer to Papadmalji Agro Foods IPO RHP for detailed Information.

paragraphs: Incorporated in December 2017, Papadmalji Agro Foods Limited is engaged in the manufacturing and marketing of papads and related food products. The Company manufactures a range of products including hand-made papads, machine-made papads, machine-made ready-to-fry papads, rice papads (Khichiya), vrat-special papads and moongodi. It also undertakes white-label manufacturing of hand-made papads for clients and trades in cereal pellets under its own brand. The Company combines traditional hand-made production with semi-automated and automated machinery for dough preparation, sheeting, rolling, cutting, drying and packaging. Its products are marketed under the brands Zhakaas, Vishal, Rozana, Diamond and Papadmalji, catering to different product categories, consumer segments and distribution channels.

The Company operates through two FSSAI-licensed manufacturing units in Bikaner, Rajasthan, with its Gharsisar unit also certified under ISO 22000:2018. Hand-made papads are produced through the Batara–Batari model, under which contractors supervise women workers engaged in home-based hand rolling. The Company sources key raw materials such as urad dal, moong dal, spices and edible oils primarily from domestic markets in Rajasthan. Its products are distributed through general trade, modern trade, quick-commerce platforms and its direct-to-consumer website.

The Company has established a pan-India distribution network comprising distributors and wholesalers and had a presence across 21 states and 3 Union Territories as of March 31, 2026. It also supplies products to an independent merchant exporter, through whom its products reach selected Middle Eastern markets. Since 2018, the Company has also been supported by an equity investment from India Customer Insight Fund, a SEBI-registered Alternative Investment Fund.
As of March 31, 2026, the Company had a total workforce of 118 employees across management, finance, production, quality control, sales and marketing, supply chain, maintenance and other functions.
strengths: Focus on purity, health and wellness.
Wide range of products with diverse variants.
Experienced Promoters and professional management team.
Extensive and well-established sales and distribution network.
Women-led hand-made production model supporting traditional manufacturing.
Multi-channel presence across general trade, modern trade, quick commerce and direct-to-consumer channels.

It also undertakes white-label manufacturing of hand-made papads for clients and trades in cereal pellets under its own brand. The Company combines traditional hand-made production with semi-automated and automated machinery for dough preparation, sheeting, rolling, cutting, drying and packaging. Its products are marketed under the brands Zhakaas, Vishal, Rozana, Diamond and Papadmalji, catering to different product categories, consumer segments and distribution channels.

The Company operates through two FSSAI-licensed manufacturing units in Bikaner, Rajasthan, with its Gharsisar unit also certified under ISO 22000:2018. Hand-made papads are produced through the Batara–Batari model, under which contractors supervise women workers engaged in home-based hand rolling. The Company sources key raw materials such as urad dal, moong dal, spices and edible oils primarily from domestic markets in Rajasthan. Its products are distributed through general trade, modern trade, quick-commerce platforms and its direct-to-consumer website.

The Company has established a pan-India distribution network comprising distributors and wholesalers and had a presence across 21 states and 3 Union Territories as of March 31, 2026. It also supplies products to an independent merchant exporter, through whom its products reach selected Middle Eastern markets. Since 2018, the Company has also been supported by an equity investment from India Customer Insight Fund, a SEBI-registered Alternative Investment Fund.

As of March 31, 2026, the Company had a total workforce of 118 employees across management, finance, production, quality control, sales and marketing, supply chain, maintenance and other functions.

faqs.question: How to apply in Papadmalji Agro Foods IPO through Zerodha?
faqs.answer: Zerodha customers can apply online in Papadmalji Agro Foods IPO using UPI as a payment gateway. Zerodha customers can apply in Papadmalji Agro Foods IPO by login into Zerodha Console (back office) and submitting an IPO application form. Steps to apply in Papadmalji Agro Foods IPO through Zerodha Visit the Zerodha website and login to Console. Go to Portfolio and click the IPOs link. Go to the ' Papadmalji Agro Foods IPO ' row and click the 'Bid' button. Enter your UPI ID, Quantity, and Price. Submit IPO application form. Visit the UPI App (net banking or BHIM ) to approve the mandate. Visit Zerodha IPO Application Process Review for more detail.
